claim: In a regression setting (neural-network force fields predicting atomic forces), ensemble/committee uncertainty correlates strongly with actual error on in-distribution validation data: Spearman rho = 0.90 (committee) and 0.91 (bootstrap-aggregation ensemble).
stance_target: the audited paper's claim/implication that ensemble sigma is generally a distance signal rather than an error signal (rho=0.07)
scope_conditions: regression (force-field energies and forces), SrTiO3 bulk system, validation data drawn from the same distribution as training data (near/in-distribution)
quoted_support: the Spearman correlation coefficient between uncertainty and error over the validation data set is 0.90 for the committee and 0.91 for the bootstrap-aggregation ensemble.

claim: The same paper shows this uncertainty-error correlation degrades substantially when evaluated on genuinely out-of-distribution structures (4x1 surface reconstructions structurally distinct from the bulk training data), especially at the level of individual atoms rather than aggregated layers.
stance_target: the audited paper's implicit premise that OOD/extrapolation regimes behave differently from in-distribution regimes for uncertainty-error correlation
scope_conditions: regression, SrTiO3 4x1 surface reconstruction (OOD relative to bulk training data)
quoted_support: the correlation between uncertainty and error within the topmost layers is not good enough to identify the most problematic atoms directly... the skill of the uncertainty in the forces as a proxy for error improves with the cardinal of the set of atoms considered: it is still good when applied to a whole layer, but less so for individual atoms.

claim: The paper explicitly argues that raw input-space distance to training data is too simplistic a proxy for uncertainty in high-dimensional regression because such models extrapolate with overwhelming probability, favoring model-internal (ensemble/committee) uncertainty over naive distance metrics.
stance_target: whether input-distance and model-internal-uncertainty are equivalent constructs
quoted_support: it is common to find this issue framed in terms of interpolation vs. extrapolation with respect to the training data; that is, however, too simplistic a picture, since regression models in high dimensionality will extrapolate with overwhelming probability.

claim: The paper frames a well-behaved uncertainty estimator as one whose correlation with error enables active learning (identifying high-uncertainty, presumably high-error regions to prioritize for retraining), directly linking uncertainty quality to error-informativeness as the primary desideratum, not distance-awareness per se.
stance_target: conceptual framing of what makes an uncertainty estimate useful
quoted_support: Ideally, the uncertainty in a prediction made by a ML model correlates with the error, because that allows for active learning approaches to iteratively improve the prediction capabilities of a model by identifying regions of high uncertainty (and therefore presumably high error) and retraining the model
